newsitem.title: INDIA: Bombay shares end off lows, index down about 2.0 pct.
newsitem.headline: Bombay shares end off lows, index down about 2.0 pct.

text.p: Frontline Bombay stocks ended slightly above their day's lowest levels on Wednesday, but a majority of them suffered losses by close, dealers said.
A bearish sentiment led to nervous market conditions, with major players jumping onto the selling bandwagon, they said.
"The trend is irreversibly down," said Ramesh Damani, a member-broker at the Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE). "The clouds of recession are hanging over the market."
The BSE's 30-share index dived 85 points in mid-session, but then recovered to a provisional 2,749.41 close, off 48.59 points or 1.74 percent from Tuesday's close.
Participants said shares of Larsen & Toubro and Indian Petrochemicals Corp Ltd were hammered by speculators.
Both figured in the list of the top five actively traded stocks at the BSE,with L&T crashing 14.0 rupees, or 6.9 percent to 189.50. IPCL fell 7.50 rupees to 101 rupees.
Some scattered buying by domestic institutions came up by close of trade on Wednesday, but it was limited to select stocks, traders said.
Gujarat Ambuja Cement which bore the brunt of selling pressure in recent sessions ended 4.0 rupees higher at 195.0. M&M and TELCO also figured among the auto stocks that closed up.
Dealers said the market fall was accompanied by delivery based selling which indicated that panicky investors were also pressing sales in the market.
The 50-stock National Stock Exchange (NSE) index skidded 22.54 points, or 2.79 percent, to end at 786.46 provisional.
ACC fell 10.70 rupees to 920.0, SBI 3.50 to 205.75, TISCO 2.50 to 147.0, Reliance 2.0 to 178.50, ITC 2.75 to 262.25, Bajaj Auto 46.0 to 710.0 and Indian Hotels 22.20 to 618.50.
M&M was up 9.0 at 275.50, TELCO 4.50 at 294.50 and Grasim 1.0 at 370.0.
